verified_claims: Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana (ICML 2005) quote is accurate: with a calibration set under about 200-1000 cases, Platt scaling beat isotonic regression for all nine learning methods (checked in the downloaded text, nmc.txt line 1381).

Kull, Silva Filho & Flach (AISTATS 2017, PMLR v54) is real. Beta calibration includes the identity map, and the abstract says logistic calibration 'can easily uncalibrate a perfectly calibrated classifier'.

Vovk & Petej, 'Venn-Abers predictors' (arXiv:1211.0025, UAI 2014) is real. It guarantees calibration under IID. The log-loss minimax merge p = p1/(1-p0+p1) is equation (10) in the paper, so the report did not need to derive it.

The three-outcome Kelly formula with pushes, f = (b*p_w - p_l)/(b*(p_w+p_l)), is correct (I re-derived it). The claim that fractional-Kelly fraction c keeps about c(2-c) of maximum growth is a correct quadratic approximation.

Walsh & Joshi (arXiv:2303.06021, Machine Learning with Applications 16, 2024, NBA data) exists. A 2025 corrigendum (MLWA vol. 19, doi 10.1016/j.mlwa.2025.100627) reports feature-engineering errors and says the conclusion stands. The report is right not to quote ROI figures: they differ across versions (+110.42% vs 2.98%; +34.69% vs -35.17%).

Benter (1994) R-squared values (public 0.1218, fundamental 0.1245, combined 0.1396) match the actamachina annotated reproduction. Alpha and beta are fit by maximum likelihood on fundamental estimates from a separate sample of races.

Hubacek, Sourek & Zelezny (IJF 2019) says, in the downloaded text, that increasing correlation with the bookmaker 'consistently decreased the profit'. Sir & Hubacek, 'Beating the market with a bad predictive model' (arXiv:2010.12508) exists and argues an inferior model can profit.

Baker & McHale (IJSP 5(3), 2016) eq. 3 matches the report: lambda = delta^2/(delta^2 + ((b+1)/b)^2 sigma^2). Table 1 numbers match: Jeffreys prior 29.23 vs 29.17; Beta(3,3) 5.63 vs 5.93. The paper also says that a Bayes rule with a correct prior needs no shrinkage.

Uhrin, Sourek, Hubacek & Zelezny (arXiv:2107.08827, IMA J. Management Math. 2021) tested horse racing, basketball and football/soccer. Plain Kelly and max-Sharpe 'often led to ruin'. Tuned fractional Kelly was best or near-best. Maximum bet limits were inconclusive.
The Buchdahl quotes via Pinnacle Odds Dropper are accurate (a practitioner source): SD about 1.00 for even-money P&L vs about 0.1 for CLV; 'perhaps as few as just 50' bets vs several thousand.
Beggy, Kim, Mucaj & Nordell (Wharton student research journal, Spring 2023) exists. Full Kelly went bankrupt in 100% of scenarios.

The toy simulation is real. Re-running sim.py with its fixed seed reproduced the reported rows exactly: c=0/tau=0.3 gave 4 bets and -0.0010; c=0/tau=1.0 gave 31 bets and -0.0207 with drawdown probability 0.06; c=1/tau=0.3 gave 63 bets and +0.1679; c=1/tau=1.0 gave 144 bets and +0.5530 with drawdown probability 0.35.

Repo facts check out: staking.js defaults to a 0.25 Kelly multiplier and has slateRiskCheck; nfl-devig.js implements Shin; stakeFor in nfl-execution-edge.js allow-lists only 'execution', so model-sourced bets get zero units. The memory note records the 51.38% break-even, -2.28 CLV and 78% adverse moves.

Repos: ip200/venn-abers (MIT, 207 stars, pushed 2026-09); ptocca/VennABERS (MIT, 79 stars); betacal/python (MIT, 32 stars); aangelopoulos/conformal-prediction (MIT); marcopeix/conformal-ts (BSD-3-Clause); cvxgrp/kelly_code (GPL-3.0).

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Lisandro79/BeatTheBookie: license not checked, verify before borrowing.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Checked: it is GPL-3.0 (last push 2021-10). Copying its code into the app would bring GPL obligations, so it belongs next to cvxgrp/kelly_code on the do-not-copy list. Use the Kaunitz et al. paper only.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Walsh & Joshi found that Kelly only worked with a well-calibrated model.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Unverified. None of the abstract versions I checked mention Kelly (arXiv v4, Bath portal, preprint). A secondary search summary suggests the 2025 corrigendum says Kelly can fail even with a well-calibrated model. The ROI figures changed a lot between versions, so treat this paper as weak, NBA-only support for calibration-first model selection, not for Kelly.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Uhrin et al.: a drawdown constraint performed about the same as fractional Kelly.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Misstated. The paper ranks distributionally robust Kelly as safest in every experiment and the drawdown constraint as second safest and efficient. Fractional Kelly was best or near-best on the chosen metrics. 'About the same' blurs a risk-vs-return ranking, and robust Kelly is left out.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: With no real edge, a skeptical prior shuts betting down on its own, with no gate (from the simulation).
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The numbers reproduce, but the simulation does not test the rule the report recommends. It uses a symmetric N(0, tau^2) prior on c, no a or b market coefficients, a correctly specified logistic truth, no pushes, no CLV likelihood and independent games. The recommended rule instead uses a half-normal, non-negative c with a Laplace approximation. With that prior the posterior mean of c is always positive, even when the true edge is zero, and a Laplace approximation is not valid at the c = 0 boundary. So 'stakes shrink toward zero on their own' is unproven for the actual recommendation.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Deflate tau for the number of specifications searched (F06; Harvey & Liu backtest haircut).
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: No source given, and no established method exists. Harvey & Liu haircut Sharpe ratios and p-values for multiple testing; they do not give a mapping to a prior scale. This is the author's opinion, not a cited method.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: aangelopoulos/conformal-prediction supplies conformal predictive CDF snippets.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Unverified. The repo exists (MIT), but it mainly contains interval and risk-control notebooks. I did not confirm it has conformal predictive distribution (Vovk et al. 2019) code. marcopeix/conformal-ts has 3 stars, so it is too immature to rely on beyond reading.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: CLV carries about 10x less noise per bet than P&L, so it is a faster skill signal.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The quote is accurate but it comes from a practitioner, and it assumes you consistently beat the close. It does not justify treating CLV evidence and outcome evidence as independent likelihoods for the same parameter (see recommendations).

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Grossman-Zhou drawdown cushion (GF03) to add alongside slateRiskCheck.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Nothing named Grossman or Zhou exists in staking.js today. It would be new work, not an existing feature. The report also misses that safeStakeFor has a binary calibrationPassed flag, which is another gate the redesign must remove.

recommendations_to_drop_or_change: Drop the 'second likelihood for c from CLV, multiplied with the outcome likelihood' step. The CLV slope (how the close moves given s) is a different parameter from the outcome slope c. Both are measured on the same games, so multiplying the Gaussians double-counts evidence. Keep CLV as a separate, anytime-valid monitor that can scale the Kelly multiplier kappa down.

Remove the half-normal (non-negative) truncation on c, or at least do not fit it with a Laplace approximation. Use a symmetric prior centred at 0 and let the model bet only when the posterior-mean EV on the model's side is positive. The Gridiron evidence (-2.28 CLV, 78% adverse moves) points to negative c; truncation would hide exactly that failure while the posterior mean of c stays above zero.

Stop stacking shrinkage layers without justification: posterior mean, then Baker-McHale lambda, then quarter Kelly, then a 2% cap. Baker & McHale (2016) say lambda is for plug-in or unbiased estimates and that a Bayes rule with a correct prior needs no extra shrinkage. Pick one uncertainty-shrinkage mechanism, either the posterior or lambda. Pre-register a single kappa, and tune it only on walk-forward folds that are never used for the final evaluation.

Make nested out-of-sample fitting explicit (a lookahead guard). The authority logistic, conformal CDF, Venn-Abers and beta calibrator must each be fit only on base-model predictions that were themselves made walk-forward, never on in-sample fits (Benter's own requirement). With about 270 games a season, do not chain conformal CDF, Venn-Abers, beta calibration and the authority logistic together. Use one calibration layer, for example the authority logistic on s with the conformal margin CDF as the only probability source.

Do not fit c on closing-line signals and then apply it to Tuesday or opening quotes. The historical s is computed against the close; at serving time s is computed against an earlier quote, which is a different distribution (the memory note says the opener path is dead). Either fit on quotes from the same timestamp (quote tape only, so authority stays near zero until that sample grows) or restrict model bets to near-close quotes. This belongs in the recommendation, not buried in open questions.
Soften or remove the Walsh & Joshi Kelly claim and the Uhrin 'drawdown about the same' wording. Mention that distributionally robust Kelly was the safest strategy.

Before claiming the rule turns itself off with no gate, re-run the simulation with the actual recommended specification: a and b market coefficients, the chosen prior on c, pushes, correlated slates, and a true c that is negative, to match Gridiron's CLV. Test prior misspecification too.
corrected_summary: What survives verification. (1) At about 270 games a season, calibrate with Platt, beta calibration (Kull et al., AISTATS 2017; it includes the identity map, while logistic calibration can uncalibrate a perfectly calibrated classifier) or Venn-Abers (Vovk & Petej, UAI 2014; IID guarantee; merge p = p1/(1-p0+p1), eq. 10), not isotonic (Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005, quote verified). The guarantees assume exchangeability, which NFL season-to-season drift violates. (2) Learn the model's weight against the market on held-out data with a logit combination (Benter 1994: public R^2 0.1218, fundamental 0.1245, combined 0.1396, fit by maximum likelihood on fundamental estimates from a separate sample; taken from the verified annotated reproduction). (3) Kelly on a posterior-mean win probability is Bayes-optimal under log utility. Baker & McHale's shrinkage lambda = delta^2/(delta^2 + ((b+1)/b)^2 sigma^2) is for plug-in estimates or a wrong prior (IJSP 2016, Table 1 verified: 29.23 vs 29.17 with a correct prior, 5.63 vs 5.93 with a wrong one). Use one of the two, not both stacked on quarter Kelly. (4) The three-outcome Kelly with pushes, f = (b p_w - p_l)/(b(p_w+p_l)), is correct, and p_push should come from a margin PMF with key-number mass. (5) Plain Kelly and max-Sharpe often ruin; tuned fractional Kelly is best or near-best; distributionally robust Kelly is safest; a drawdown constraint is second safest; max bet limits are inconclusive (Uhrin et al. 2021). Beggy et al. (Wharton student journal, 2023) found full Kelly bankrupt in 100% of scenarios. (6) Decorrelating from the bookmaker raises profit at fixed accuracy (Hubacek et al., IJF 2019), but Gridiron's decorrelation is a fade of informed money (-2.28 CLV, 78% adverse moves), so grade it on CLV and outcomes. (7) Per Buchdahl (practitioner source), CLV has about one-tenth the per-bet SD of P&L, so use it as a separate anytime-valid monitor (Shafer, JRSS A 2021, testing by betting). Do not multiply it into the outcome likelihood as independent evidence. Recommended rule, corrected. Take p_m by Shin devig of the quote actually available at decision time. Compute s = logit(p_model) - logit(p_m), where p_model comes from base-model predictions that were themselves walk-forward. Fit logit(p) = a + b*logit(p_m) + c*s weekly with tight priors on a and b and a SYMMETRIC pre-registered prior on c, using only games graded before t. Fit on the same quote timestamp you bet on, or bet only near the close, because training on closes and serving on openers is a distribution mismatch. Stake = min(cap, kappa * f_Kelly3(posterior-mean probabilities)) with one pre-registered kappa. Remove the zero-unit rule for model-sourced bets in stakeFor and the calibrationPassed flag in safeStakeFor. Keep slateRiskCheck. Log a decision tape and grade CLV against a declared close. The toy simulation reproduces, but it tests a simpler, correctly specified rule, so 'no gate needed' is unproven for the real specification until it is re-simulated with a negative true c, pushes and correlated slates. Code to borrow (ports only): ip200/venn-abers (MIT, active), ptocca/VennABERS (MIT, cross-check), betacal/python (MIT). Do not copy cvxgrp/kelly_code or Lisandro79/BeatTheBookie (both GPL-3.0). All of this is small enough for pure JS, so nothing needs installing. Treat Walsh & Joshi only as weak NBA evidence that calibration-based selection beats accuracy-based selection. Its Kelly claim is unverified and its ROI numbers changed across versions and the corrigendum.
